note: Post-UTME Current Affairs round 1: Nigeria and world general knowledge for university screening tests (officeholders, constitution, history, economy, elections, security, geography, Africa/world, sports, ICT). Facts checked September 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's President, sworn in on 29 May 2023, is
questions.explanation: Bola Ahmed Tinubu of the APC took the oath of office on 29 May 2023 after winning the February 2023 election.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Vice-President of Nigeria who took office alongside the President in May 2023 is
questions.explanation: Senator Kashim Shettima, a former Governor of Borno State, has been Vice-President since 29 May 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The President of the 10th Senate of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Senator Godswill Akpabio was elected Senate President when the 10th National Assembly was inaugurated in June 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Speaker of the House of Representatives in the 10th National Assembly is
questions.explanation: Rt. Hon. Tajudeen Abbas, from Kaduna State, has been Speaker since June 2023; Benjamin Kalu is his deputy.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Deputy Senate President of the 10th Senate is
questions.explanation: Senator Barau Jibrin of Kano State is Deputy Senate President; Benjamin Kalu is Deputy Speaker of the House.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chief Justice of Nigeria sworn in on 22 August 2024 is
questions.explanation: Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun succeeded Justice Olukayode Ariwoola and is the second woman to hold the office.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In October 2025 a new Chairman of INEC was sworn in to succeed Prof. Mahmood Yakubu. He is
questions.explanation: Prof. Joash Amupitan, a law professor and SAN, took office as INEC Chairman on 23 October 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Olayemi Cardoso was confirmed as CBN Governor by the Senate in September 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Inspector-General of Police of Nigeria as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Kayode Egbetokun was appointed Inspector-General of Police in June 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The National Security Adviser to the President as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Nuhu Ribadu, pioneer chairman of the EFCC, has been National Security Adviser since June 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Secretary to the Government of the Federation as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Senator George Akume, a former Governor of Benue State, is Secretary to the Government of the Federation.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chief of Staff to President Tinubu is
questions.explanation: Femi Gbajabiamila, Speaker of the 9th House of Representatives, became Chief of Staff in June 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's Minister of Education as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Dr Maruf Tunji Alausa became Minister of Education in October 2024; Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad is Minister of State.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Nyesom Wike, former Governor of Rivers State, has been FCT Minister since August 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare is
questions.explanation: Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate has led the health ministry since August 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's Minister of Works, in charge of federal highways such as the Lagos-Calabar coastal road, is
questions.explanation: Engr. Dave Umahi, former Governor of Ebonyi State, is Minister of Works.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In April 2026 the President replaced Wale Edun as Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy with
questions.explanation: Taiwo Oyedele, who had chaired the Presidential Committee on Fiscal Policy and Tax Reforms, took over the finance ministry in April 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's Minister of Foreign Affairs as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Ambassador Yusuf Maitama Tuggar has been Minister of Foreign Affairs since August 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Minister of Information and National Orientation as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Mohammed Idris Malagi is Minister of Information and National Orientation; Dele Alake is Minister of Solid Minerals.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's Minister of Defence as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Mohammed Badaru Abubakar, former Governor of Jigawa State, is Minister of Defence; Bello Matawalle is Minister of State.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, has been Attorney-General of the Federation since August 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chief of Defence Staff appointed in October 2025 is
questions.explanation: General Olufemi Oluyede became Chief of Defence Staff on 24 October 2025, replacing General Christopher Musa.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chief of Army Staff appointed in October 2025 is
questions.explanation: Major-General Waidi Shaibu was named Chief of Army Staff in the October 2025 change of service chiefs.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chief of Naval Staff appointed in October 2025 is
questions.explanation: Rear Admiral Idi Abbas took over as Chief of Naval Staff in October 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chief of Air Staff appointed in October 2025 is
questions.explanation: Air Vice Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke became Chief of Air Staff in October 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited appointed in April 2025 is
questions.explanation: Bayo Ojulari replaced Mele Kyari as head of NNPC Limited on 2 April 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Director-General of NAFDAC as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Prof. Mojisola Christianah Adeyeye has headed NAFDAC since 2017; the late Dora Akunyili led it from 2001 to 2008.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian who serves as Deputy Secretary-General of the United Nations is
questions.explanation: Amina J. Mohammed, a former Nigerian Minister of Environment, has been UN Deputy Secretary-General since 2017.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian who is Director-General of the World Trade Organisation is
questions.explanation: Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became WTO Director-General in March 2021, the first woman and first African in the post.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In March 2025 the President declared a state of emergency in one state, suspending its governor, deputy governor and House of Assembly for six months. The state is
questions.explanation: Emergency rule was declared in Rivers State on 18 March 2025 and a sole administrator ran the state until September 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The governor re-elected in the Anambra State election of 8 November 2025 is
questions.explanation: Prof. Charles Soludo of APGA won a second term with over 422,000 votes, taking all 21 local government areas.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Executive Chairman of the EFCC appointed in October 2023 is
questions.explanation: Ola Olukoyede succeeded Abdulrasheed Bawa as EFCC chairman in October 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Governor of Lagos State as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: Babajide Sanwo-Olu has governed Lagos State since May 2019 and was re-elected in 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Nigeria is made up of 36 states, the Federal Capital Territory and how many local government areas?
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution lists 774 local government areas across the 36 states, plus six area councils in the FCT.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The Nigerian Senate has how many members?
questions.explanation: Three senators from each of the 36 states plus one for the FCT gives 109 senators.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The House of Representatives in Nigeria has how many members?
questions.explanation: The House has 360 members elected from federal constituencies; together with the 109 senators the National Assembly has 469 members.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: A legislature with two chambers, like Nigeria's National Assembly, is described as
questions.explanation: Bicameral means two chambers: the Senate and the House of Representatives.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The constitution currently in force in Nigeria is the Constitution of
questions.explanation: The 1999 Constitution came into force on 29 May 1999 with the return to civilian rule; it has since been amended several times.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Making laws for the federation is the main duty of which arm of government?
questions.explanation: The legislature (National Assembly) makes laws; the executive implements them and the judiciary interprets them.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The third tier of government in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: Nigeria has three tiers: federal, state and local government.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu and Imo states make up which geopolitical zone?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's six geopolitical zones are North-Central, North-East, North-West, South-East, South-South and South-West.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Since the Not Too Young To Run Act of 2018, the minimum age to contest for President of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The 2018 amendment reduced the age for President from 40 to 35 and for the House of Representatives from 30 to 25.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Under the 1999 Constitution, the longest any one person may serve as President of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: A presidential term is four years and no one may be elected more than twice, so the maximum is eight years.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The minimum age at which a Nigerian may register and vote in an election is
questions.explanation: Every citizen of 18 years and above who registers with INEC is entitled to vote.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The head of the judiciary in Nigeria is the
questions.B: President of the Court of Appeal
questions.explanation: The Chief Justice of Nigeria heads the Supreme Court and the whole judicial arm.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Nigeria's seat of government officially moved from Lagos to Abuja in
questions.explanation: The FCT was created in 1976, but the formal movement of the capital to Abuja took place on 12 December 1991 under General Babangida.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: A bill passed by both chambers of the National Assembly normally becomes law when
questions.explanation: Presidential assent turns a bill into an Act; if assent is withheld, a two-thirds vote of each chamber can override the veto.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The power to remove (impeach) the President of Nigeria for gross misconduct belongs to the
questions.explanation: Impeachment is a legislative process requiring a two-thirds majority of each chamber of the National Assembly.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Elections into local government councils in a state are conducted by the
questions.explanation: Each state has its own State Independent Electoral Commission (SIEC) for council elections; INEC conducts federal and state elections and those in the FCT area councils.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: In July 2024 the Supreme Court ruled that allocations from the Federation Account must be paid directly to
questions.explanation: The judgment on local government autonomy stopped governors from holding council funds in joint accounts and ordered direct payment to democratically elected councils.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The principle that federal appointments must reflect the diversity of Nigeria's states and ethnic groups is called
questions.explanation: Federal character, in Section 14 of the Constitution, guards against domination of government by any one group.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Since 1979 Nigeria has practised which system of government?
questions.explanation: The First Republic used the parliamentary (Westminster) system; since the 1979 Constitution Nigeria has run an executive presidential system.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The official residence and office of the President of Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The Presidential Villa at Aso Rock in Abuja has housed Nigeria's presidents since 1991; Dodan Barracks was used in Lagos.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The Constitution allows the Supreme Court of Nigeria to have the Chief Justice and not more than how many other justices?
questions.explanation: Section 230 fixes the Supreme Court at the Chief Justice and up to 21 justices.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Nigeria was first divided into 12 states in 1967 by
questions.explanation: Gowon replaced the four regions with 12 states in May 1967; Abacha's 1996 creation brought the total to the present 36.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: The Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The Constitution makes the President the Commander-in-Chief; the Chief of Defence Staff is the most senior serving officer.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.topic: Nigeria: Constitution and Structure of Government
questions.q: Who presides over a joint sitting of the Senate and the House of Representatives?
questions.explanation: The Senate President presides over joint sittings, such as the presentation of the annual budget.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria gained independence from Britain on
questions.explanation: Independence came on 1 October 1960; Nigeria became a republic exactly three years later.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria became a republic, replacing the Queen with a Nigerian Head of State, in
questions.explanation: The Republican Constitution took effect on 1 October 1963 with Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe as ceremonial President.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Northern and Southern Protectorates were amalgamated into one Nigeria in 1914 by
questions.explanation: Lord Lugard carried out the amalgamation on 1 January 1914 and became the first Governor-General of Nigeria.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The name 'Nigeria' was first suggested in 1897 by
questions.explanation: Flora Shaw, a journalist with The Times of London who later married Lord Lugard, coined the name from the River Niger.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's first and only Prime Minister was
questions.explanation: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa led the government from 1957 until the January 1966 coup in which he was killed.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's first President, a ceremonial head of state from 1963, was
questions.explanation: Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe was Governor-General from 1960 and President from 1963 to 1966.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's first executive President, elected in 1979, was
questions.explanation: Alhaji Shehu Shagari of the NPN was the first President with executive powers under the 1979 Constitution.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's first military Head of State, after the coup of January 1966, was
questions.explanation: Major-General Johnson Aguiyi-Ironsi took power in January 1966 and was killed in the counter-coup of July 1966.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian Civil War was fought between
questions.explanation: The war began on 6 July 1967 and ended on 15 January 1970 with the surrender of Biafra.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Head of State of Nigeria throughout the civil war was
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon led Nigeria from 1966 to 1975 and declared 'no victor, no vanquished' at the end of the war.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Democracy Day, celebrated on 12 June, marks the presidential election of 1993 widely believed to have been won by
questions.explanation: The 12 June 1993 election won by Chief M.K.O. Abiola of the SDP was annulled by General Babangida; 12 June became Democracy Day in 2018.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria returned to civilian rule on 29 May 1999 with the swearing-in of
questions.explanation: Chief Olusegun Obasanjo won the 1999 election and served two terms until 2007.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The military leader who handed over power to elected civilians on 29 May 1999 was
questions.explanation: General Abdulsalami Abubakar took over after Abacha's death in June 1998 and completed the transition within a year.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which leader ruled Nigeria as a military Head of State from 1983 to 1985 and later as elected President from 2015 to 2023?
questions.explanation: Buhari came to power in the December 1983 coup and won the 2015 and 2019 elections as a civilian.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The military Head of State assassinated in the failed coup of 13 February 1976 was
questions.explanation: General Murtala Mohammed was killed in Lagos in the coup led by Lt-Col. Dimka; Obasanjo succeeded him.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Who became President of Nigeria in May 2010 following the death of President Umaru Yar'Adua?
questions.explanation: Vice-President Goodluck Jonathan was sworn in on 6 May 2010 and won the election of 2011.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian flag was designed in 1959 by
questions.explanation: Taiwo Akinkunmi, then a student in London, won the national competition for the flag design.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: On the Nigerian flag, the green bands stand for
questions.explanation: Green represents agriculture and the land's fertility; the white band represents peace and unity.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In May 2024 Nigeria re-adopted its old national anthem, which begins with the words
questions.explanation: The National Anthem Act 2024, signed on 29 May 2024, restored 'Nigeria, We Hail Thee', which had been used from 1960 to 1978.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: On Nigeria's coat of arms, the Y-shaped white wavy bands on the black shield represent
questions.explanation: The two bands meeting on the shield stand for the Niger and the Benue meeting at Lokoja; the black shield is Nigeria's fertile soil.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The motto written under Nigeria's coat of arms is
questions.explanation: The coat of arms carries the motto 'Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress'.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's oldest university, founded in 1948, is the
questions.explanation: The University College, Ibadan, opened in 1948 as a college of the University of London and became a full university in 1962.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The first indigenous university in Nigeria, opened in 1960 by Dr Nnamdi Azikiwe, is the
questions.explanation: UNN opened in October 1960; UI was founded earlier but as a college of the University of London.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The naira replaced the Nigerian pound as the national currency on
questions.explanation: Nigeria changed to the decimal naira and kobo on 1 January 1973.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) was established in 1973 by the government of
questions.explanation: Gowon set up the NYSC by decree in May 1973 to promote national unity after the civil war.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's last national population census, held in 2006, put the population at about
questions.explanation: The 2006 census recorded about 140 million people; a new census has been postponed several times since 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria celebrated its 65th independence anniversary on 1 October
questions.explanation: Independence was in 1960, so the 65th anniversary fell on 1 October 2025 and the 66th on 1 October 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The first woman to serve as Chief Justice of Nigeria, sworn in in 2012, was
questions.explanation: Justice Aloma Mariam Mukhtar was CJN from 2012 to 2014; Justice Kekere-Ekun in 2024 became the second woman in the office.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1986, was
questions.explanation: Professor Wole Soyinka won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 1958 novel 'Things Fall Apart', one of the most widely read African books, was written by
questions.explanation: Chinua Achebe's 'Things Fall Apart' tells the story of Okonkwo and the coming of colonial rule to Umuofia.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The port city annexed by Britain in 1861, becoming the first British colony in what is now Nigeria, was
questions.explanation: Lagos was annexed as a Crown colony in 1861; the protectorates of the interior came later in the 1880s and 1890s.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: General Sani Abacha's creation of six new states in 1996 raised the number of states in Nigeria to
questions.explanation: Abacha created Bayelsa, Ebonyi, Ekiti, Gombe, Nasarawa and Zamfara on 1 October 1996, bringing the total to 36.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The National Minimum Wage Act signed in July 2024 fixed Nigeria's minimum monthly wage at
questions.explanation: President Tinubu signed the Act on 29 July 2024, raising the minimum wage from ₦30,000 to ₦70,000.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The petrol subsidy in Nigeria was ended by the President's announcement 'subsidy is gone' on
questions.explanation: The removal was announced in President Tinubu's inaugural speech on 29 May 2023, and pump prices rose sharply the same week.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery, the largest single-train refinery in the world, is located at
questions.explanation: The 650,000 barrels-per-day refinery in the Lekki Free Zone was commissioned on 22 May 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The refining capacity of the Dangote Refinery is about
questions.explanation: At 650,000 barrels per day it exceeds the combined capacity of Nigeria's four government-owned refineries.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: When the National Bureau of Statistics rebased Nigeria's GDP in July 2025, it changed the base year from 2010 to
questions.explanation: The 2025 rebasing used 2019 as the new base year and put the 2024 GDP at about ₦372.8 trillion.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: After the 2025 GDP rebasing, which sector moved up to become the third-largest in Nigeria's economy, pushing crude oil and gas to fifth place?
questions.explanation: The rebased figures ranked real estate third behind crop production and trade, with crude petroleum and natural gas fifth.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The government agency that publishes Nigeria's inflation, unemployment and GDP figures is the
questions.explanation: The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) is Nigeria's official statistical agency.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Under the tax reform laws signed in 2025, the Federal Inland Revenue Service was replaced from January 2026 by the
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Revenue Service (Establishment) Act 2025 created the NRS to collect federal taxes and non-tax revenue in place of FIRS.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 merged the education tax, NASENI and NITDA levies into a single 4% charge on company profits called the
questions.explanation: The 4% Development Levy replaces several separate levies and funds bodies such as TETFund, NELFUND and NASENI.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), created by the Student Loans Act of 2024, gives students
questions.explanation: NELFUND lends tuition and upkeep money to students in public tertiary institutions, repayable after graduation and employment.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Petroleum Industry Act of 2021 turned the national oil company into a limited liability company known as
questions.explanation: NNPC Limited was incorporated in 2021 and unveiled in July 2022 as a commercial company under the Petroleum Industry Act.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria became a member of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) in
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined OPEC in 1971; the organisation's headquarters is in Vienna, Austria.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The institution that issues Nigeria's currency and manages the country's monetary policy is the
questions.explanation: The Central Bank of Nigeria, established in 1958, issues the naira and sets the monetary policy rate.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The digital form of the naira launched by the Central Bank in October 2021 is called the
questions.explanation: The eNaira, launched on 25 October 2021, is a central bank digital currency, not a cryptocurrency.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The BVN that every bank customer in Nigeria must have stands for
questions.explanation: The Bank Verification Number, introduced by the CBN in 2014, links a customer's biometrics to all their bank accounts.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The National Identification Number (NIN) is issued by the
questions.explanation: NIMC enrols citizens and residents and issues the 11-digit NIN used for SIM cards, passports and banking.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The agency that protects depositors by insuring the money kept in Nigerian banks is the
questions.explanation: The NDIC pays insured depositors when a bank fails; the SEC regulates the capital market instead.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The body that regulates Nigeria's capital market, including the stock exchange, is the
questions.explanation: The SEC regulates the capital market; shares are traded on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Lekki Deep Sea Port, Nigeria's first deep seaport, was commissioned in January 2023 in
questions.explanation: The port in the Lekki Free Zone, Lagos, can berth much larger vessels than Apapa and Tin Can Island.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Second Niger Bridge links Asaba in Delta State with
questions.explanation: The 1.6 km bridge, opened to traffic in 2022-2023, relieves the old Niger Bridge between Asaba and Onitsha.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 700-kilometre coastal highway under construction from Lagos is planned to end in
questions.explanation: The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway runs through the coastal states to Calabar in Cross River State.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Lagos Blue Line, the first rail line of the Lagos light-rail network opened in 2023, runs from Marina to
questions.explanation: The first phase of the Blue Line runs from Marina to Mile 2; the Red Line, opened in 2024, runs towards Agbado.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's biggest export and main source of foreign exchange is
questions.explanation: Crude oil and gas provide most of Nigeria's export earnings, although agriculture employs more people.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigeria LNG plant, which exports liquefied natural gas, is located on
questions.explanation: NLNG's six trains (with a seventh under construction) are on Bonny Island in Rivers State.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Ajaokuta Steel Company, Nigeria's largest steel project, is located in
questions.explanation: Ajaokuta is in Kogi State, near the iron-ore deposits of Itakpe.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Kainji Dam, Nigeria's oldest large hydroelectric dam, is built on the
questions.explanation: Kainji Dam in Niger State was completed in 1968 on the River Niger; Jebba and Shiroro dams came later.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: President Tinubu's overall development programme is known as the
questions.explanation: 'Renewed Hope' was the slogan of the 2023 campaign and the name of the administration's agenda.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The busiest airport in Nigeria, serving Lagos, is named after
questions.explanation: Murtala Muhammed International Airport is in Ikeja, Lagos; Abuja's airport is named after Nnamdi Azikiwe.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Mobile network operators such as MTN, Airtel and Glo are regulated in Nigeria by the
questions.explanation: The NCC licenses telecom operators and sets rules on tariffs, SIM registration and quality of service.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's first satellite, launched in September 2003, was
questions.explanation: NigeriaSat-1, an earth-observation satellite built for NASRDA, was launched from Russia in 2003.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), under which trading started on 1 January 2021, has its secretariat in
questions.explanation: The AfCFTA Secretariat is in Accra; the agreement was signed in Kigali in 2018 and Nigeria signed in 2019.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The unit into which one naira is divided is the
questions.explanation: One naira is made up of 100 kobo.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Under INEC's revised timetable, Nigeria's presidential and National Assembly elections of 2027 hold on
questions.explanation: INEC moved the 2027 elections forward under the Electoral Act 2026: presidential and National Assembly polls on 16 January 2027, the first January presidential election since 1999.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Under the revised INEC timetable, the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections of 2027 hold on
questions.explanation: Governorship and State Assembly elections were fixed for Saturday 6 February 2027, three weeks after the presidential poll.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The new electoral law signed in 2026 that changed the timing of the 2027 elections repealed the
questions.explanation: The Electoral Act 2026 repealed and replaced the Electoral Act 2022 that governed the 2023 general election.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In Nigerian elections, BVAS stands for
questions.explanation: The BVAS device accredits voters by fingerprint or face and uploads polling-unit results.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The INEC portal on which polling-unit result sheets are uploaded for the public to view is called
questions.explanation: IReV, the INEC Result Viewing portal, displays scanned Form EC8A results from polling units.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's most recent presidential election, won by Bola Tinubu, was held on
questions.explanation: The presidential and National Assembly elections held on 25 February 2023; governorship elections followed on 18 March 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In the 2023 presidential election, the candidate who came second was
questions.explanation: INEC declared Tinubu (APC) winner with Atiku Abubakar (PDP) second and Peter Obi (Labour Party) third.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which of these states holds its governorship election outside the general election cycle (an 'off-cycle' election)?
questions.explanation: Eight states vote off-cycle because of past court judgments: Anambra, Bayelsa, Edo, Ekiti, Imo, Kogi, Ondo and Osun.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Governor Charles Soludo of Anambra State belongs to which political party?
questions.explanation: The All Progressives Grand Alliance has governed Anambra since 2006; Soludo was re-elected on its platform in November 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The full name of INEC is the
questions.explanation: INEC, the Independent National Electoral Commission, was established in 1998 to organise federal and state elections.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The exercise through which INEC registers new voters between elections is called
questions.explanation: Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) allows citizens who turn 18 or relocate to register or transfer their registration.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The party that has controlled the federal government since 2015 is the
questions.explanation: The All Progressives Congress won the presidency in 2015 (Buhari) and 2023 (Tinubu).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chairman of INEC is appointed by the President subject to confirmation by the
questions.explanation: The Constitution requires Senate confirmation of the INEC Chairman after consultation with the Council of State.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: To be declared winner of a presidential election in Nigeria at the first ballot, a candidate needs the highest number of votes and at least one-quarter of the votes in
questions.B: two-thirds of the states and the FCT
questions.explanation: Section 134 requires the highest votes plus not less than 25% in at least two-thirds of the 36 states and the FCT.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The annulled presidential election of 12 June 1993 was conducted under the military government of
questions.explanation: General Babangida's government annulled the election; he 'stepped aside' in August 1993 for the Shonekan interim government.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In Nigerian elections, the card a registered voter presents at the polling unit is the
questions.explanation: The Permanent Voter Card (PVC) is issued by INEC after registration and is read by the BVAS on election day.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The agency responsible for investigating advance-fee fraud, money laundering and other financial crimes in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission was established in 2003.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The ICPC, set up in 2000, deals mainly with
questions.explanation: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission investigates bribery and abuse of office in the public service.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian agency that arrests drug traffickers and destroys cannabis farms is the
questions.explanation: The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency was established in 1989.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The paramilitary agency that protects pipelines, power installations and other critical national infrastructure is the
questions.A: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
questions.explanation: The NSCDC also supervises private guard companies and protects schools under the Safe Schools initiative.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The body that enforces traffic laws and issues driver's licences and number plates on Nigerian highways is the
questions.explanation: The Federal Road Safety Corps was established in 1988.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's domestic intelligence and internal security service is the
questions.D: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
questions.explanation: The DSS handles internal security; the NIA handles foreign intelligence and the DIA military intelligence.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The agency that fights human trafficking in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons was established in 2003.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The agency that coordinates the response to floods, building collapses and other disasters in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The National Emergency Management Agency coordinates disaster response; state agencies are called SEMAs.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian Defence Academy, which trains officers for the Army, Navy and Air Force, is located in
questions.explanation: The NDA has been in Kaduna since 1964.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the three services of the Nigerian Armed Forces?
questions.explanation: The Armed Forces are the Army, Navy and Air Force; the police is a separate civil force under the Inspector-General.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigeria Immigration Service is responsible for
questions.explanation: The NIS issues Nigerian passports, controls the borders and regulates the stay of foreigners; Customs collects duties.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Western Nigeria Security Network launched by the six South-West states in January 2020 is popularly called
questions.explanation: Amotekun ('leopard' in Yoruba) supports the police in Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Osun and Oyo states.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria has a single national police force headed by the
questions.explanation: Policing is on the exclusive legislative list, so there is one Nigeria Police Force under the Inspector-General; states cannot yet run their own.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The agency that registers and regulates food, drugs, cosmetics and bottled water in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: NAFDAC, set up in 1993, gives products their registration numbers; SON sets standards for other goods.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The rivers Niger and Benue meet at
questions.explanation: The confluence is at Lokoja in Kogi State, which was also Lugard's first administrative capital.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The highest point in Nigeria, Chappal Waddi, is located in
questions.explanation: Chappal Waddi (about 2,419 m) is in the Gashaka-Gumti area of Taraba State near the Cameroon border.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The largest state in Nigeria by land area is
questions.explanation: Niger State covers about 76,000 square kilometres; Lagos is the smallest state by area.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The country on Nigeria's western border is
questions.explanation: Benin lies to the west, Niger to the north, Chad to the north-east and Cameroon to the east.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria shares its eastern border with
questions.explanation: Cameroon borders Nigeria to the east, from the Lake Chad area down to the Bakassi peninsula.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Zuma Rock, the landmark on the Abuja-Kaduna road, actually stands in
questions.explanation: Zuma Rock is in Madalla, Niger State, just outside the FCT boundary.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Olumo Rock, a famous tourist site and place of refuge during the 19th-century wars, is in
questions.explanation: Olumo Rock is in Abeokuta, the capital of Ogun State.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's time zone is West Africa Time, which is
questions.explanation: Nigeria is one hour ahead of Greenwich Mean Time all year round.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's southern coastline lies on the
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Guinea is part of the Atlantic Ocean; the Niger Delta opens into it.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Moving from the coast northwards, the correct order of Nigeria's vegetation belts is
questions.explanation: Rainfall decreases northwards: mangrove swamp on the coast, then rainforest, then Guinea and Sudan savanna, then Sahel in the far north.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Argungu International Fishing Festival is held in
questions.explanation: Argungu is on the Sokoto River in Kebbi State; the festival dates from 1934.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is in
questions.explanation: The grove on the outskirts of Osogbo was listed by UNESCO in 2005 and hosts the annual Osun festival.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's first UNESCO World Heritage Site, listed in 1999, is the Sukur Cultural Landscape in
questions.explanation: Sukur, in the Mandara Mountains of Adamawa State, was listed in 1999; Osun-Osogbo followed in 2005.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Eyo masquerade festival is associated with
questions.explanation: Eyo, with its white-robed masquerades, is a Lagos Island festival held to honour a departed chief or oba.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The annual Durbar, a procession of horsemen marking the end of Ramadan and Eid, is best known in
questions.explanation: The Kano Durbar, recognised by UNESCO in 2024, is held at the Emir's palace; Katsina, Zaria and Bida also hold durbars.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The month-long Calabar Carnival, called 'Africa's biggest street party', is held in
questions.explanation: The carnival runs through December in Calabar, capital of Cross River State.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The dry, dusty north-east wind that blows from the Sahara over Nigeria between November and March is the
questions.explanation: The harmattan brings cool mornings, dust haze and dry skin in the dry season.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Lake Chad is shared by Nigeria, Chad, Niger and
questions.explanation: The four countries of the Lake Chad Basin are Nigeria, Niger, Chad and Cameroon.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian city nicknamed the 'Coal City' is
questions.explanation: Coal was mined at Enugu from 1909; Port Harcourt is the 'Garden City' and Jos the 'Tin City'.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's most populous city and commercial capital is
questions.explanation: Lagos, the capital until 1991, remains the largest city and the centre of commerce and finance.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's film industry is popularly known as
questions.explanation: Nollywood is one of the largest film industries in the world by number of films; Kannywood is the Hausa-language industry in Kano.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The three most widely spoken indigenous languages in Nigeria are
questions.explanation: Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba are recognised as the major national languages alongside English, the official language.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The town on Nigeria's border with Benin Republic that was a major slave port and now hosts a 'Point of No Return' monument is
questions.explanation: Badagry in Lagos State has slave-trade relics and the 'Point of No Return' on Gberefu Island.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The headquarters of the African Union is in
questions.explanation: The AU, which replaced the OAU in 2002, is headquartered in Addis Ababa.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Chairperson of the African Union Commission elected in February 2025 to succeed Moussa Faki is
questions.explanation: Djibouti's long-serving foreign minister Mahmoud Ali Youssouf defeated Kenya's Raila Odinga after seven rounds of voting.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: ECOWAS, the Economic Community of West African States, was founded in 1975 by the Treaty of
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Lagos was signed on 28 May 1975; the ECOWAS Commission is now based in Abuja.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The three countries that formally left ECOWAS in January 2025 to form the Alliance of Sahel States are
questions.explanation: The three military-led states announced their withdrawal in January 2024 and it took effect on 29 January 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Secretary-General of the United Nations as at 2026 is
questions.explanation: António Guterres of Portugal has been UN Secretary-General since January 2017; his second term runs to the end of 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian who served as President of the African Development Bank from 2015 to 2025 is
questions.explanation: Dr Akinwumi Adesina, a former Minister of Agriculture, completed two five-year terms at the AfDB.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Mauritanian economist who became President of the African Development Bank on 1 September 2025 is
questions.explanation: Dr Sidi Ould Tah was elected in May 2025 with over 76% of the votes and succeeded Akinwumi Adesina.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The pope elected on 8 May 2025, the first from the United States, took the name
questions.explanation: Cardinal Robert Prevost became Pope Leo XIV after the death of Pope Francis in April 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2025 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the Venezuelan opposition leader
questions.explanation: María Corina Machado was honoured on 10 October 2025 for her struggle for democratic rights in Venezuela.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The President of the United States inaugurated on 20 January 2025 is
questions.explanation: Donald Trump returned to the White House as the 47th President after winning the November 2024 election.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The President of Ghana who took office in January 2025 is
questions.explanation: John Mahama won the December 2024 election and returned to office for a second, non-consecutive term.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The first G20 summit held on African soil took place in November 2025 in
questions.explanation: South Africa held the G20 presidency in 2025 and hosted the leaders' summit in Johannesburg.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2025 United Nations climate conference, COP30, was hosted in Belém by
questions.explanation: COP30 was held in Belém, at the mouth of the Amazon, in November 2025; COP29 was in Baku, Azerbaijan.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The head of the Commonwealth of Nations, of which Nigeria has been a member since 1960, is
questions.explanation: King Charles III succeeded Queen Elizabeth II as Head of the Commonwealth in 2022; the secretariat is in London.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The headquarters of OPEC is in
questions.explanation: OPEC has been headquartered in Vienna since 1965.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The United Nations, which Nigeria joined in October 1960, has its headquarters in
questions.explanation: The UN headquarters is in New York; Geneva hosts many UN agencies such as the WHO.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The ECOWAS Parliament and the ECOWAS Court of Justice sit in
questions.explanation: Nigeria hosts the ECOWAS Commission, Parliament and Court in Abuja.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The largest country in Africa by land area is
questions.explanation: Algeria became Africa's largest country when Sudan split in 2011; Nigeria is the most populous.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In January 2025 Nigeria was admitted as a partner country of which grouping of major emerging economies?
questions.explanation: Brazil, as chair, announced Nigeria's admission as a BRICS partner country on 17 January 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The World Health Organisation has its headquarters in
questions.explanation: The WHO is based in Geneva, Switzerland; its Africa regional office is in Brazzaville.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In the WAFCON final of 26 July 2025 in Rabat, the Super Falcons came from 2-0 down to beat the hosts Morocco
questions.explanation: Nigeria won 3-2 to lift a record tenth Women's Africa Cup of Nations title, the team's 'Mission X'.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Super Falcons' victory at the 2024 WAFCON (played in 2025) was Nigeria's
questions.explanation: It was Nigeria's tenth WAFCON title in 13 editions of the tournament.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian named Player of the Tournament at the 2024 WAFCON was
questions.explanation: Captain Rasheedat Ajibade won the award; goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie was named best goalkeeper.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The coach who led the Super Falcons to the 2024 WAFCON title was
questions.explanation: Justine Madugu, who took charge in 2024, was named Coach of the Tournament.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: At the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations hosted by Morocco, the Super Eagles finished in
questions.explanation: Nigeria won the third-place match; the final was played between Senegal and Morocco.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Player of the Tournament at the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations was
questions.explanation: Senegal's Sadio Mané was named best player; Morocco's Brahim Díaz won the Golden Boot.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be co-hosted by Kenya, Uganda and
questions.explanation: The three East African countries will stage the 2027 tournament together.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2026 FIFA World Cup, the first with 48 teams, was hosted jointly by the United States, Canada and
questions.explanation: The tournament ran from 11 June to 19 July 2026 across the three North American countries.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2026 FIFA World Cup was won by
questions.explanation: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the final at the MetLife Stadium, New Jersey.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria missed the 2026 World Cup after losing the CAF play-off final in November 2025 on penalties to
questions.explanation: After a 1-1 draw in Rabat, DR Congo won the shoot-out 4-3; the Super Eagles had beaten Gabon 4-1 in the semi-final.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Malian who coached the Super Eagles during the 2026 World Cup qualifiers was
questions.explanation: Eric Chelle was appointed Super Eagles head coach in January 2025.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The 2025 men's Ballon d'Or was won by the Paris Saint-Germain forward
questions.explanation: Dembélé won the award on 22 September 2025 after PSG's first Champions League title; Lamine Yamal was second.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Super Eagles have won the Africa Cup of Nations how many times?
questions.explanation: Nigeria won in 1980 (Lagos), 1994 (Tunisia) and 2013 (South Africa).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian who set the women's 100 metres hurdles world record of 12.12 seconds in 2022 is
questions.explanation: Tobi Amusan set the record in the semi-final of the 2022 World Championships in Oregon and went on to win gold.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's first individual Olympic gold medal was won in the long jump at Atlanta 1996 by
questions.explanation: Chioma Ajunwa jumped 7.12 m to win gold; the 'Dream Team' also won the football gold at the same Games.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: At the 2025 Grammy Awards, the Nigerian singer who won Best African Music Performance for 'Love Me JeJe' was
questions.explanation: Tems won her second Grammy in February 2025 with 'Love Me JeJe', a reworking of Seyi Sodimu's 1997 hit.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's under-17 team, the Golden Eaglets, has won the FIFA U-17 World Cup a record
questions.explanation: The Golden Eaglets won in 1985, 1993, 2007, 2013 and 2015.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Nigeria's senior women's basketball team is known as
questions.explanation: D'Tigress is the women's basketball team; D'Tigers are the men, and the Falconets are the under-20 women's footballers.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The national stadium in Abuja was renamed in 2019 in honour of
questions.explanation: President Buhari renamed it the Moshood Abiola National Stadium on 12 June 2019.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Nigerian musician regarded as the creator of the Afrobeat genre is
questions.explanation: Fela Kuti developed Afrobeat in the late 1960s, blending highlife, jazz and funk with political lyrics.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Super Falcons' semi-final win at the 2024 WAFCON came against the defending champions
questions.explanation: Nigeria beat South Africa 2-1 with a 94th-minute winner from Michelle Alozie.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The part of a computer that carries out instructions and is often called its 'brain' is the
questions.explanation: The CPU processes data; the hard disk stores it and the keyboard and monitor are input and output devices.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which of these is an INPUT device?
questions.explanation: A scanner sends data into the computer; printers, monitors and speakers send information out.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: RAM is described as volatile memory because
questions.B: its contents are lost when power goes off
questions.D: it is slower than a hard disk
questions.explanation: Random Access Memory holds data only while the computer is on; unsaved work disappears when power is lost.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: On a Windows computer, the keyboard shortcut Ctrl + C is used to
questions.explanation: Ctrl + C copies, Ctrl + X cuts, Ctrl + V pastes and Ctrl + Z undoes the last action.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The keyboard shortcut Ctrl + S in most programs is used to
questions.explanation: Saving often with Ctrl + S protects your work from being lost.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which application is best suited for preparing a class budget with automatic totals?
questions.explanation: Excel is a spreadsheet; its cells and formulas add up figures automatically.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In the web address https://www.jamb.gov.ng, the letters 'www' stand for
questions.explanation: The World Wide Web is the system of linked web pages accessed through the internet.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: One byte is made up of how many bits?
questions.explanation: Eight bits make a byte; about 1,024 bytes make a kilobyte and 1,024 kilobytes make a megabyte.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The symbol that must appear in every e-mail address, as in student@gmail.com, is
questions.explanation: The @ sign separates the user name from the domain name of the mail provider.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: A message that pretends to come from your bank and asks you to click a link and enter your PIN is an example of
questions.explanation: Phishing tricks people into revealing passwords, PINs or card details; banks never ask for these by e-mail or SMS.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Which of these is an operating system?
questions.explanation: Android, Windows, iOS and Linux are operating systems; the others are application programs.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The physical parts of a computer that can be touched, such as the mouse and the monitor, are called
questions.explanation: Hardware is the equipment; software is the set of instructions that runs on it.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: A program used to visit websites, such as Chrome, Firefox or Safari, is called a
questions.explanation: A browser displays web pages; Google is a search engine that you use inside a browser.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The saying 'garbage in, garbage out' (GIGO) means that
questions.explanation: A computer processes exactly what it is given, so incorrect data leads to incorrect results.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Computers store and process all data using the binary number system, which has the base
questions.explanation: Binary uses only the digits 0 and 1, matching the on and off states of electronic circuits.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The World Wide Web was invented in 1989 by
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee created the web at CERN; the internet itself is older.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Software that detects and removes viruses and other malicious programs is called
questions.explanation: Antivirus programs scan files and downloads for malware and should be kept up to date.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: Storing your files on services such as Google Drive so you can open them from any device is known as
questions.explanation: Cloud storage keeps files on remote servers reached over the internet.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: A strong password should
questions.C: be the same on every site
questions.D: be shared with a friend for safety
questions.explanation: Long passwords that combine letters, numbers and symbols, and that are not reused, are hardest to guess.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: In a computer-based test like the UTME, the candidate chooses answers mainly with the
questions.explanation: CBT candidates click options with a mouse (or touchpad) and may use the keyboard's letter keys.
